extraction.name: MATHVISTA
extraction.description: A benchmark designed to combine challenges from diverse mathematical and visual tasks, consisting of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA).
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.citeAs: Lu et al., MATHVISTA: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts, ICLR 2024
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was compiled by collecting nine MathQA datasets and reviewing over 70 VQA datasets to select 19 containing math-related instances. Three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA) were created. Heuristic rules were used to automatically select examples with numeric answers or quantity words, followed by manual labeling by expert annotators. All questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and refined through a rigorous review process with majority voting.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 28 existing multimodal datasets (9 math-targeted, 19 VQA) and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation. Heuristic rules were applied to filter VQA datasets for math-related instances. Disagreements in annotations were resolved through discussion among the review team.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Heuristic rules were designed to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning from VQA datasets based on numeric answers or quantity words. Expert annotators manually labeled these examples. Metadata such as question type, answer type, task category, grade level, visual context, and required reasoning skills were annotated.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: All questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields. A two-step process was employed: initially, each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers. Discrepancies were resolved through discussion among the entire review team to ensure consensus. Inter-annotation consistency rate was 99.2%.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotation consistency was measured using Fleiss Kappa score (0.775 for labeling mathematical reasoning) and a general consistency rate of 99.2% for the newly collected 736 questions, where only 6 exhibited disagreements.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields; Human performance baseline annotators had a high school diploma or higher and satisfactory annotating history on Amazon Mechanical Turk.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 (used for answer extraction with >99.5% accuracy)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The test set answer labels will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination. An online evaluation platform will be maintained. The benchmark is part of an ongoing research process, with commitments to maintain datasets and evolve the leaderboard in response to community feedback and new models.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to facilitate the development of mathematical reasoning systems in visually intensive scenarios and evaluate research progress of LLMs and LMMs. It highlights the critical role of such benchmarks in developing general-purpose AI agents for real-world tasks.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset covers diverse visual contexts and mathematical skills but may have gaps in representation of certain types of mathematical problems. Annotations lack a unified format due to heterogeneity of sources.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Dataset coverage may have gaps in certain mathematical problems and visuals. Scalability and generalizability to other domains are concerns. Annotations lack a unified format. The study focused exclusively on recent and prominent models. Gaps exist in representation of specific domains like science and college-level math compared to textual-only datasets.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. Evaluation of mathematical reasoning capabilities of foundation models in visual contexts.
